campaign: as pulse-peer-discount-confirm: 21 workloads x 5 scenarios x attack rates 1, 3, 6, 12, 24 per second, 525 trials, each control (15 s idle) -> benign exec (15 s) -> attack (15 s) on one container; fresh campaign on fresh traffic. system_changes_under_test.tripwire_live: tripwire A1 inside the worker (sentinel_pulse/rules/tripwire.py), masks of the other workers over the peer exchange
system_changes_under_test.shared_writes_off_loop: NFS writes of the worker from background threads (pipeline/async_sink.py), fdatasync + POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED every 30 s, STATUS written asynchronously
system_changes_under_test.local_decision_stream: decisions also on each worker's local disk; the alert bridge, RCA and campaign read that copy
system_changes_under_test.bridge_retry: a failed episode push is retried (3 attempts, 0.5 s apart)
system_changes_under_test.rca_from_alertmanager: RCA builds a case per alert episode that Alertmanager delivered (bridge triggers.jsonl), ML or tripwire

arms.A_ml: the live previews of the ML (decision column candidate_alert_preview)
arms.T_tripwire: the live tripwire alerts (decision column tripwire_alert, tripwire_status = judged)
arms.S_system: A and T as parallel streams, definitions of rule-integration-v1 amendment 2 (trial detected when any stream alerts inside [start, start + 15 s]; alert time = earliest stream alert; normal alerts of one container (pod_uid, container) merged across streams into episodes when less than 15 s apart)

expectations.S_system_primary: recall >= 95 %, precision >= 95 %, idle-control positive <= 5 %, p95 kernel -> first alert (window end) <= 3 s. Met = all four. Wilson 95 % CI reported
expectations.A_ml_primary: the same four, reported as the replication of Pulse 5.27
expectations.S_burden: normal span = selection end -> capture end, campaign span excluded (burden_levers.campaign_span); episodes per replica-hour of the ML window table; reported with a workload-clustered bootstrap 95 % CI (10,000 draws). The claim 'the tripwire adds little burden' needs the upper 95 % bound of S - A <= 0.25 episodes/replica-hour (R6 primary: +0.066 [+0.020; +0.133])
expectations.tripwire_live_vs_offline: scripts/analysis/novel_syscalls.py on the same run with the same reference span and exec set; per judged window, live alert == offline alert in >= 99.9 % of windows; every disagreement attributed (late peer reference window, pending window, other)

reported_without_threshold: kernel -> recipient on the push path for S (episodes opened by either stream), registered subset and all rates; same join as alert_delivery_latency.py

frame lag (preview_emitted_at - window_end) p50 / p95 / p99 / max per worker, cadence gaps per worker, shared-writer waits and longest write; against pulse-peer-discount-confirm (8-10 cadence gaps per worker)
bridge: failed pushes, retries, episodes never delivered by push (previous run: 13 failed pushes, 6 of 5,181 episodes)

RCA: attack trials with a case, top-1 ranking, kernel -> case latency, cases opened by tripwire alerts, attack trials grouped after the benign case (previous runs 56/525 and 44/524; expected near 0 with the distinct path)
zombie processes under Tetragon after the run (expected 0)
recall by attack rate for A, T and S
statistics: Wilson 95 % CI for rates; workload-clustered bootstrap 10,000 draws for burden and paired differences; percentile p95 as in rule_comparison.py for arms, nearest rank as in alert_delivery_latency.py for delivery
